_help: 212 Kids games. A game is a list of rounds; each round asks questions from "items".

Round types: yesno, tap, count, pizza, freeze, missing, search, cross, memory, bubble, oddout, match, sort, hidden, pick, say, elf, wish, present, sounds, listen and blend. See the top of kids/game.js for every option.
A round can use a shared question pool: { "pool": "fruits-what" }. Pools are in "pools".
Each play picks a random set of questions: "per_play" by level (6 to 10), or the round's own "per_play" (1 to 10). "split": true shares that number across a game's rounds.
count questions: "count": how many to put in the basket. "count_max" (by level) skips bigger numbers: Pre-K 1-5, K 1-7, Grades 1-4 1-10.
pizza questions: mode "customer" (free choice; "pizza"."picks" by level) or "shopkeeper" (find the topping; "pizza"."choices" by level).

freeze questions: fruit dance to music made in code; it stops, "Freeze!", the child taps FREEZE, then the word, then "Do you like...?". "freeze"."dancers" by level; dance_seconds = random length of each dance.

missing questions (word games, tiny): the picture, the word said aloud, ONE letter missing ("at": 0 = first letter), and 2 letter tiles (the right one and "other"). Shown first letter first, then last, then middle.

search questions (word games, tiny): one puzzle = "words" (3) hidden left to right, one per row, in a grid as wide as the longest word. Pictures show what to find. Drag across a word, or tap its first and last letter.

cross questions (word games, tiny): one puzzle = "words" [across, down] that share a letter. Picture clues; every letter is given except 1 per word (Pre-K, K) or 2 (Grade 1+). Letter tiles = the missing letters + 1 extra.

worksheets: printable A4 sheets for grown-ups (kids/print.php?set=fruits): Missing Letters, Word Search, Crossword + answer pages. "words" = the set's words (up to 6 letters); "pairs" = crossword pairs (they must share a letter).
A question can be for some levels only: "levels": ["k", "1"]. Default: every level.
Item ids start at 100000 and are never reused or renumbered (one id sequence for all kids content). Next free id: 100882.

picture: a picture name drawn by the site (kids/pictures.js, see the list at its top; paint_<color>, num_1 to num_10, letter_a to letter_z, ball_red / book_blue / drum_green / robot_yellow / present_pink ...).
To use a real picture later, add "image": "kids_nov_banana.jpg" to the word (file goes in kids/images/).
To use a recorded voice later, add "audio": "100003.m4a" to an item (file goes in kids/audio/). Without it the browser voice speaks.
Every game always ends with 3 stars and its sticker. Wrong answers only wiggle ("Try again!"); after 2 tries the right one glows.

Word games (missing, search, cross) and worksheets: any theme with 3+ short words (up to 6 letters, with a picture). Food: fruits + pizza toppings (the pools named fruits-* hold both). Colors: colors-*.

memory questions (one board): flip 2 cards to find pairs. "words" + "match": picture (same picture twice) or word (picture + its word); or "pairs": [["red", "apple"]] (2 different pictures). "opinion": true = not in the teacher's accuracy (it's memory, not English).
bubble questions (Pop it): bubbles float up; pop the one the lion says ("word"). The other bubbles are other words from the same pool. Missed bubbles come back from the bottom. No timer.
oddout questions: 4 pictures ("choices"), tap the one that doesn't belong ("answer"); "after_correct" says why.

match questions (one board): drag each picture onto its pair. "mode": shadow (its gray shadow) or word (its written word); or "pairs" (drag apple onto red). A tap on a picture, then on a pair, works too.
sort questions (one board): 2 baskets ("groups": english, japanese, color, words); drag each picture into the right basket. A word must be in only one group.
hidden questions (one board): a picnic picture with things hidden around it; the lion says "Find the banana!" for each word in "find"; "others" are the extra things in the picture.
boards: how big each board is, by level (memory pairs, bubbles, match pictures, sort pictures, hidden: how many to find, hidden_things: how many things in the picture).

pick questions (Pick the written answer): the lion asks ("english"), the child taps the written sentence. "choices" = sentences, "answer" = the right one (or a list: both "Yes, I do." and "No, I don't." are right). "show": picture, or count ("count" pictures). boards.read_choices: 1 = the lion reads the sentences aloud (Pre-K, K).

say questions (Say it, mic): the lion says the word; the child says it. The microphone is OFF until a grown-up turns it on (on this device). Nothing is recorded, never graded ("opinion": true); "I said it!" always works.

elf questions (Elf Workshop): "Can I have a red ball, please?" -> tap the red ball ("word" + "color"; "choices" = picture names like ball_blue). boards.elf = how many choices. The child then says "Yes, you may! Here you are!".
wish questions (Dear Santa, one board): tap presents for your letter (boards.wish: how many; boards.wish_toys: how many toys to pick from). The child says "I want a robot!". Not in the accuracy.
present questions (Pass the Present, one board): unwrap "layers" (boards.present of them): "What color is the paper?"; inside is "toy": "What is it?" ("choices").

sounds / listen / blend (ABC phonics; sound numbers = Mike's phonics order, the sound files are the adult ones in portal/audio/phonics/): sounds = tap the letters to hear them ("sounds"); listen = hear a sound, tap its letter ("sound", "letter", "choices"); blend = tap each letter of "word" ("tiles": [letter, sound number]), then Blend.
Santa's Sack: a yesno fact question with "sack": true shows the picture as a shadow until it is answered.
Round 2 (Nov 5): every game has the GOAL BAR on top (who speaks, one short sentence, a goal picture, the child). Tap it to hear it again.
Voices: kids/audio/voices.json (made by _work/kids/audio/kids-voices/build_voice_list.py) says which file says each line. A line with no file uses the browser voice.
pizza: the child is always the shopkeeper. pizza.order = how many toppings one customer orders (per level); pizza.choices = toppings on the tray.

oddout "kind": "category" ("Which ones are the fruits?", answer = a list, tap every right one) or "color" ("Which one is green?", "color" = the swatch). Without kind: the old "which one is different?" (K and up).
memory_cards (per level): picture-picture or picture-word for the whole play. A memory question's own "card_type" (a word, or one per level) wins.
boards.bubble_speed: how fast the Pop it balloons drift (pixels a second, per level). The first question of a play has 2 balloons, then boards.bubbles.
tap "show": "shadow" = the picture is a dark shadow until it is answered (December: Guess the shadow!).
